senses.gloss: f. (v. גְּמַר II, 5) memorizing of verbal teachings, tradition.
units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 19a:19">Ab. Zar. 19ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>הנ״מ סברא אבל ג׳ מחד רבא וכ׳</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) this refers to reasoning (dialectics), but as to traditional laws (rules &c.), it is better to study only with one teacher, in order not to be confused by varying wording; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 614:6">Yalk. Ps. 614</cite>.—

<cite ref="Gittin 6b:10">Gitt. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>הא ג׳ היא וג׳ לא שמיע ליה</he> this is merely a tradition (not to be arrived at by way of reasoning) and one may not have heard that tradition (and yet be an able man).

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 33a:10">B. Mets. 33ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Metzia 33b:10">33ᵇ</cite> <he>ג׳</he> verbal study (opp. to <cite ref="M02939"><he>משנה</he></cite> which had been put to writing). Arakḥ. 29ᵃ <he>רב גַּמְרֵיה גמיר</he> (not <he>גמור</he>) Rab had his own tradition about it (had it from his teacher that the Mishnah was corrupt).

<cite ref="Eruvin 60a:17">Erub. 60ᵃ</cite> <he>ג׳ גמור זמורתא תהא</he> if it is a tradition, learn it by heart, let it be like a song (the wording of which you dare not change); <cite ref="Shabbat 106b:7">Sabb. 106ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 32b:3">Ab. Zar. 32ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Beitzah 24a:11">Bets. 24ᵃ</cite> (variously interpreted in comment.).—
<cite ref="Yoma 14b">Yoma 14ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>משמיה דג׳</he> as a tradition (without knowing the reasoning process, cmp.

ib. 33ᵃ bot. ג׳ גמירנא וכ׳); a. fr.—G’mara, that part of the Talmud containing those discussions, decisions &c. which, after the reduction to writing of the Mishnah, were the materials of verbal studies until they, too, were put to writing.—Abbrev. גמ׳, a clerical mark in the Talmud Babli editions, to indicate where the Mishnah ends, and the G’mara begins.
